title: Model loading - weights shard debug notes (Liam Chen)
content:
Context:
- Reproducing intermittent model load failures in staging (dedicated gpu pool). Failures observed when loading 8-way sharded fp16 weights for "redwood/large-algo-v1" model.
- Symptoms: some workers fail at runtime with checksum/size errors; others load fine. Suspect partial/bitflipped shards or transfer issues across S3-like gateway.

Timeline / quick notes:
- 2024-10-15 09:12: First failure observed during blue-green: 2/16 pods failed to bring up, crashloop on model load.
- 2024-10-15 09:18: Collected logs from pod-7 and pod-12. pod-7 reports "Checksum mismatch for shard 3"; pod-12 reports "Unexpected EOF while reading weights shard".
- 2024-10-15 09:45: Triggered manual download + local validation.

Commands tried (local debug):
- curl with range and verbose:
  curl -v -H "Range: bytes=0-" -o shard-00003.pt "https://s3.example.com/models/redwood/large-algo-v1/shards/shard-00003.pt"
  -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK, Content-Length: 143165576
  -> curl finishes, filesize 143165576 bytes

- sha256sum check vs manifest:
  $ sha256sum shard-00003.pt
  2b5f9c3a...  shard-00003.pt
  Manifest expected: 9f2d1a7b...  (MISMATCH)

- tried gsutil copy (objectstore behind GCS gateway):
  $ gsutil cp gs://redwood-models/large-algo-v1/shard-00003.pt ./
  Copy completed. sha256 != manifest.

- Attempted partial-range download to detect trailing zeros / truncated file:
  $ dd if=shard-00003.pt bs=1 skip=0 count=64 | xxd -l 64
  -> header bytes look OK (LMDB header-ish), but tail contains long run of 0x00 repeated -> suggests zero-padded file or sparse file problem.

- Python load attempt to reproduce load-time error:
  import torch
  state = torch.load('shard-00003.pt', map_location='cpu')
  -> EOFError: Ran out of input while unpickling file

- Compare sizes across nodes / object store buckets:
  $ ls -l shard-*.pt
  shard-00000.pt  143165576
  shard-00001.pt  143165576
  shard-00002.pt  143165576
  shard-00003.pt  143165576 (bad)
  ...
  All sizes identical but checksum differs for shard-00003 only.

Cluster observations:
- Failed pods are on node pool with older kernel version (5.10.x) vs healthy on 5.15.x. Not sure if relevant.
- Networking: occasional S3 gateway errors reported last week (https://status.s3gw/incident/887).

Hypotheses:
1) Upstream object was corrupted during upload (single bad shard).
   - Evidence: sha256 mismatch and EOF on torch.load.
   - Counter: other regions/nodes retrieve same size but same bad checksum, so corrupt object likely in bucket, not node-local.

2) Gateway edge is returning a zero-padded stream on rushy concurrent GETs causing checksum mismatch for some downloads.
   - Evidence: long run of 0x00 at tail in downloaded file. Known bug in gateway with certain range requests.
   - Test: download same object with different client (s3cmd, aws-cli) and compare.

3) On-the-fly decompression / transfer encoding mismatch (server sets incorrect Content-Encoding) -> client saved incorrect payload.
   - Evidence: curl -v showed no content-encoding set, but double-checking via aws s3api head-object might help.

Actions taken:
- Re-uploaded shard-00003.pt from local canonical copy to staging bucket with new object key suffix (shard-00003.v2.pt) and updated manifest to point there.
  -> Results: pods pulled v2 object and loaded successfully. So re-upload fixes the symptom.

- Opened JIRA-4217 to track root cause and coordinate with S3 gateway team.

- For immediate mitigation:
  - Added retry + verify-step in rollout: after object download, compute sha256 and compare with manifest; if mismatch, retry up to 3x with exponential backoff and switch to alternate replica endpoint.
  - Added sanity check in runtime: if torch.load throws EOFError, log object ETag/sha256 and fail fast with clearer message to aid debugging.

Unresolved / follow-ups:
- Confirm whether gateway had partial objects (zero-padded) during 2024-10-14..16 window. Request logs from objectstore team.
- Investigate kernel/network stack differences between failing and healthy nodes (MTU, TCP offload).
- Add server-side object checksum metadata (x-amz-meta-sha256) to enable fast validation before loading.
- Add a small integration test in release pipeline that simulates concurrent GETs of same object to detect gateway race condition.

Notes / useful snippets to paste into ticket:
- sample pod log (truncated):
  [2024-10-15T09:12:33Z] ERROR runtime.loader: failed to load shard shard-00003.pt: EOFError: Ran out of input while unpickling file
  [2024-10-15T09:12:33Z] DEBUG runtime.loader: attempted download url=https://s3.example.com/models/redwood/large-algo-v1/shard-00003.pt etag="\"a1b2c3\"" size=143165576

- sample curl head:
  $ curl -I https://s3.example.com/models/redwood/large-algo-v1/shards/shard-00003.pt
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  Content-Length: 143165576
  ETag: "a1b2c3"

- sha256s: expected=9f2d1a7b..., observed=2b5f9c3a...

Quick reproduction steps for infra team:
1) From a node in failing pool: curl -v -o /tmp/shard-00003.pt <url> && sha256sum /tmp/shard-00003.pt
2) From healthy node: do the same and compare checksums. If different, we have non-deterministic GET behavior (gateway bug).
3) Try aws s3 cp vs gsutil cp vs curl to see if behavior differs by client.

Misc thoughts (brain dump):
- Could consider multi-part upload validation on upload path (compute sha256 server-side, store as metadata).
- Temporary workaround: pin manifests to v2 copies (already did). But need to ensure clients fallback to alternate replica endpoints automatically.
- If gateway only affects certain objects, consider re-uploading all shards for that model as a batch job and rerun smoke tests.

Next steps (who/when):
- Liam: follow up with objectstore team to fetch gateway logs (+10h).
- Jordan: add checksum-verify step in rollout job (PR #678) - in progress.
- Maya: validate kernel/network differences on bpool-7 nodes and reproduce with iperf/mtr (ASAP).

End of notes.
